title: 2002 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 2002 FIFA World Cup, staged from 31 May to 30 June, was the first edition held in Asia and the first co-hosted by two nations, South Korea and Japan. Thirty-two teams were drawn into eight groups of four, with the top two from each advancing to a single-elimination knockout stage running through the round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final. It was the last World Cup to use the golden goal rule, which applied in the knockout rounds. China, Ecuador, Senegal and Slovenia all made their tournament debuts.

The group stage broke the script almost immediately: defending champions France went out without scoring a single goal, losing 1–0 to debutants Senegal, drawing with Uruguay and losing to Denmark. The more enduring story belonged to co-hosts South Korea, who under Guus Hiddink reached the semi-finals—the best-ever finish by an Asian nation and the first time a team from outside UEFA, CONMEBOL and CONCACAF had gone so far. Their run ended in a 1–0 defeat to Germany. In the third-place play-off, Turkey beat South Korea 3–2, a match opened by Hakan Şükür scoring roughly 11 seconds after kick-off, the fastest goal in World Cup history.

The final at the International Stadium Yokohama, before 69,029 spectators on 30 June, paired Germany and Brazil. It was settled in regulation, with no extra time or penalties, as Brazil won 2–0 through two Ronaldo goals (67', 79'). The opener came after Germany goalkeeper Oliver Kahn spilled a Rivaldo shot and Ronaldo struck the rebound. The win gave Brazil a record fifth title; Germany finished runners-up. Ronaldo's brace completed a personal redemption after Brazil's 1998 final defeat, and his eight goals—the tournament's most—were the highest single-tournament tally since Gerd Müller in 1970. Fittingly for an upended World Cup, the Golden Ball for best player went not to a scorer but to Kahn, the first and to date only goalkeeper to win the award, despite his error in the final.
